submission.justification: Radiator-R2 at 3 cm thickness is recommended as it provides the best pion/kaon separation (3.958 sigma) among radiators that meet all lifetime and performance constraints. While Radiator-R3 shows higher raw separation power (4.687 sigma at 3 cm), it fails the aging requirement with 40% transparency loss over the experiment's lifetime, far exceeding the 10% threshold. Radiator-R1 meets all constraints but delivers significantly lower separation (2.966 sigma at its optimal 4 cm thickness). Radiator-R2 achieves its maximum separation at 3 cm thickness, well within the 1-6 cm constraint, and maintains excellent transparency over time with only 6% loss, comfortably below the 10% requirement. This choice optimally balances performance with long-term reliability.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c
requirements.evidence: R2 achieves 3.958 sigma separation at 3 cm thickness, which is the best performance among radiators that meet all constraints. While R3 shows higher raw separation (4.687 sigma), it is excluded due to aging failure.

requirements.evidence: R2 passes the aging requirement (R2_passes_ageing_requirement = 1) with only 6% transparency loss, well below the 10% threshold (R2_transparency_loss_percent = 6, transparency_loss_requirement_percent = 10).
